title: Tasks, channels and bounded asynchronous pipelines
outcome: Build a bounded producer-consumer pipeline, join its work and explain how asynchronous scheduling differs from simultaneous CPU execution.

exercises.title: Trace the queue
exercises.task: Describe what happens when a producer fills a capacity-two buffer.
exercises.expected: The next put! waits until space is available.
exercises.answer: The consumer drains a value, allowing the producer to continue without unbounded queue growth.

exercises.title: Preserve output meaning
exercises.hint: One producer preserves this input order.
exercises.answer: Squares are emitted into the result in channel-consumption order; broader parallel pipelines need explicit ordering.

exercises.title: Inject a failure
exercises.task: Set fail_after=0 on a nonempty list.
exercises.hint: The finally block still closes the channel.
exercises.answer: No shortened result is mislabeled success; joining propagates the producer failure.

exercises.title: Drain a closed channel
exercises.task: Put 7 into a channel, close it, then collect it.
exercises.expected: The buffered value is still returned.
exercises.hint: Closure means no future puts, not immediate deletion.
exercises.answer: Buffered values can be drained before iteration terminates.

exercises.title: Identify an unsupported generalization
exercises.task: Explain what can go wrong if an arbitrary consumer callback throws.
exercises.expected: A producer can remain blocked without coordinated cancellation.
exercises.hint: Inspect who closes and who waits.
exercises.answer: The bounded example proves its stated simple consumer path; a generic pipeline needs both failure directions designed.

exercises.title: Transfer to file processing
exercises.task: Specify identifiers and completion evidence for concurrent files.
exercises.expected: Use stable file IDs and explicit per-file outcomes.
exercises.hint: A printed line is not a durable acknowledgment.
exercises.answer: Define ordering, retries and partial failure semantics before introducing concurrency.
